Audrey shrugged.

<atomic>"Kyra, you can skip rocks?" I turned to see Olivia behind me. My face grew hot as I casually dropped the rocks I had been holding.</atomic>
<atomic>"Yeah, sort of," I mumbled. Olivia was good at everything she tried. When she wasn't winning track medals, she was starring in the school musical or leading the debate club.</atomic>
<atomic>"I've never been able to!" Olivia said helplessly. "It looks so cool, though. I wish I could!"</atomic>

<atomic>Seeing Olivia's smiling face, I realized that maybe being able to skip rocks wasn't a worthless talent after all. I leaned down and picked up a rock I had dropped, holding it out for her.</atomic>
<atomic>"Want to practice?" I asked. Olivia nodded eagerly and joined me at the water's edge.</atomic>
She concentrated, aimed, and threw the rock. It sank immediately with a loud plunk.

<atomic>"It's all in the wrist," I said, standing a little straighter and skipping another stone; that one made it to the middle of the pond. We took turns, giggling with joy when one of Olivia's rocks finally skipped once.</atomic>

Lisa breathed a sigh of relief when she and Kim finally landed.
